title: fix(platform-objects,cli): translate the Setup app's runtime-contributed navigation, and move the coverage verdict onto the merged app metadata (#5750)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#5750

## Premise re-verification (measured item by item on `origin/main` `487a197b5`; the card was measured at `9f22801` and main has moved since)

All three facts still hold:

- `nav_packages` has **exactly 1 occurrence** under `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/`, and it sits under `apps.studio.navigation`; `nav_approval_delegations` / `nav_webhooks` / `nav_http_deliveries` are **zero hits** each. A control probe (`nav_users`) on the same file returns 1, so those zeros are real and not a broken path filter.
- The hardcoded English labels are still at source: `plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts:86`, `plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:103` and `:104`.
- `scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json`: examples 89 + 451 + 120 = 660, and **every first-party package still records 0**.

## Both halves implemented

### Half 1 — the four labels

`nav_packages` was translated under a different app's namespace. Setup looks it up at `apps.setup.navigation.nav_packages`, misses, and falls back to the author's `'Packages'` literal. Two apps carrying the same nav id is normal, so the Setup entry is added and the `studio` one is left alone. The other three had no translation in any locale and are now added.

### Half 2 — closing the handoff (the part that matters)

New gate `pnpm check:app-nav-i18n` (`packages/cli/scripts/check-app-nav-i18n.mjs`, wired into `lint.yml`): it boots the real composition, merges the navigation contributions through the same `applyNavContributions` path the `/api/v1/meta/app` read uses, and asserts that **after the merge** every nav id carries a label in every locale. This is exactly what the card's repro script does, running in CI.

It lives in `packages/cli` for a reason: "who serves this path" is a question about the **composed runtime** (AGENTS.md, Route & surface ownership). `cli` is the composition root `os dev` / `os serve` assemble from, and the only workspace package that depends on all ten Setup nav contributors at once. A gate in `platform-objects` could not import those plugins at all (the dependency runs the other way) and would only ever measure the empty shell.

## Four more the new gate found — invisible to a single-locale repro

`nav_capabilities` / `nav_settings_localization` / `nav_settings_company` / `nav_datasources` were translated in `zh-CN` **only**, so `ja-JP` and `es-ES` showed English there too. The issue's repro ran under zh alone, which is why these never surfaced. All eight ids are now labelled in all four locales — this is not scope creep, it is what the new gate requires in order to be green.

## Red path exercised, all three kinds (beyond `--self-test`)

**First — before the fix** (8 ids across 4 locales, each naming the id, the locale, the contributing package and the literal that would be fallen back to):

```
check-app-nav-i18n: 4 problem(s)

  • apps.setup.navigation — locale `zh-CN` has no label for 4 runtime-merged nav id(s):
      nav_packages contributed by @objectstack/setup (SETUP_APP + SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS) — author's literal "Packages"
      nav_approval_delegations contributed by @objectstack/plugin-approvals — author's literal "Delegations (OOO)"
      nav_webhooks contributed by @objectstack/plugin-webhooks — author's literal "Webhooks"
      nav_http_deliveries contributed by @objectstack/plugin-webhooks — author's literal "HTTP Deliveries"
```

That `zh-CN` row is **exactly** the four the card names — the new gate independently reproduced the card's premise.

**Second — single-label ablation** (delete `nav_webhooks` from zh-CN, rebuild, run):

```
check-app-nav-i18n: 1 problem(s)

  • apps.setup.navigation — locale `zh-CN` has no label for 1 runtime-merged nav id(s):
      nav_webhooks contributed by @objectstack/plugin-webhooks — author's literal "Webhooks"
```

**Third — contributor ablation**, which is the anti-false-green direction, and the direction is inverted: fewer merged ids means fewer ids checked, so a plugin that silently stops contributing would make this gate **greener**, not redder. Replacing `plugin-webhooks` with a contributor that registers nothing:

```
check-app-nav-i18n: 1 problem(s)

  • @objectstack/plugin-webhooks landed NO `setup` navigation id. Either it stopped contributing
    (then remove it from CONTRIBUTORS in this script, in the same PR) or its registration silently
    no-ops — which would make this gate greener, not redder, by giving it fewer ids to check.

  Nothing was compared: the coverage verdict is only meaningful over a COMPLETE
  composition, so it was not attempted.
```

All three ablations were reverted; after the fix the gate is green:

```
check-app-nav-i18n: OK (10 contributor(s), 53 merged `setup` nav id(s), 4 locale(s), every id labelled in every locale).
```

## The two dead rationales are rewritten

The card is right that moving the coverage verdict makes those two comments false. Both are rewritten in this PR, and each now records what was wrong before — one sentence, "gated by the coverage ratchet", written in two files that pointed at each other while nobody stood on the ground between them:

- `app-nav-translation-parity.test.ts` read "Those labels are gated by the coverage ratchet";
- `packages/platform-objects/scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts` read "Their gate is the coverage ratchet (`scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs`), baselined at 0 for this package".

`scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs` also gains a "what this gate cannot see" paragraph in its own header, so the next reader does not have to re-derive it. **Note the ratchet's 0 is not wrong** — it is true for this package's **static** declared surface; it simply does not own the runtime half.

## The gate's boundaries, stated plainly in its header rather than implied

1. **One composition is a subset of what can be contributed.** Some entries are conditional — `plugin-auth` contributes `nav_sso_providers` only when an external IdP is wired — so a label this run never merged is a label this run never judged.
2. **No reverse direction.** Studio asserts "no translation without a declaring nav item"; that cannot be copied here, because from a single runtime composition a **dead** key and a **gated-off** key are indistinguishable, and asserting it would delete the latter's translations.

Each boundary became an unassigned finding, both actually filed:

- objectstack-ai/objectstack#6659 — `nav_sso_providers` has no label in any of the four locales, and is the one entry this gate structurally cannot see (concrete defect, left unlabeled for PM triage).
- objectstack-ai/objectstack#6660 — four dead `apps.setup.navigation` keys (`nav_approval_processes` / `nav_metadata` / `nav_verifications` / `nav_device_codes`) with zero declaring nav items repo-wide (`finding` label, observation-class).

## Direction 3 of the card is NOT decided here

"Should plugin nav `label` values be allowed as bare English literals, or must they go through an i18n key?" — per the ruling that is not mine to decide. This implementation **does not need** to answer it: labels stay bare literals, translations continue to live in `platform-objects`' `apps.setup.navigation`, and the gate holds under either authoring contract.

## Verification

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm lint` | pass (`EXIT=0`) |
| `pnpm exec turbo run typecheck --filter=@objectstack/platform-objects --filter=@objectstack/cli` | 56 tasks, all pass |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects test` | 9 files / 275 tests pass |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli test` | 94 files / 978 tests pass |
| `pnpm check:i18n` | OK (all 9 packages in sync) |
| `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` | OK (12 configs, 660 baselined, none new) — **this one was already green and is NOT evidence** |
| `pnpm check:app-nav-i18n` | OK (10 contributors, 53 merged nav ids, 4 locales) |
| `pnpm check:nul-bytes` | OK (6208 files, no raw control bytes) |
| `pnpm check:doc-authoring` / `check:workflow-status-functions` / `check:published-files` / `check:role-word` / `check:adr-anchors` | all pass |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated --reconcile-only` | OK (19 check: + 13 gen: scripts, all classified) |

The `check:i18n-coverage` row is kept deliberately unchanged: it was green throughout the whole defect and is green now. **The thing that moved is the new gate.**

## One widening of the declared file surface

The claim comment's declared surface did not include `packages/cli/`. The new gate has to live in a package that can see the complete composition, and that is only `packages/cli`: this adds `packages/cli/scripts/check-app-nav-i18n.mjs` plus one script line in `packages/cli/package.json`, and for the same reason touches the root `package.json` (root script) and `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (wiring it into the job that carries the required gates). `scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json` is **unchanged** — this PR does not move any static config's count.

## Changeset

`.changeset/setup-nav-runtime-i18n-coverage.md`, `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`. Fixing four (in fact eight) user-visible labels across three non-English locales is a user-visible change, so this takes a changeset rather than `skip-changeset`.
